text: Samba is a town, municipal committee, and administrative headquarter of the Samba district in Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, located in the disputed Kashmir region. It has its own railway station on the Jammu-Delhi railway line. Samba is situated at 32°34′N 75°07′E﻿ / ﻿32.57°N 75.12°E﻿ / 32.57; 75.12 and has an average elevation of 384 m (1,260 ft). It lies in the Shivalik Hills alongside National Highway 1-A on the bank of the Basantar River, 40 km (25 mi) from Jammu. The district borders Udhampur District to the north, Kathua District to the east, the Tehsils Jammu and Bishnah of Jammu District to the west, and the International Border with Pakistan to the south. According to Census India 2011, the Samba Municipal Committee has a population of 12,700, of which 6,979 (55%) are males and 5,721 (45%) are females. There are 1,365 children under seven years old, or 10.75% of the population, and 2,566 households in the city. By caste, 71% are from the general caste, 28.57% are from the schedule caste, and 0.04% are from the schedule tribes. Hinduism is the dominant religion, with Christians, Muslims, and Sikhs as minorities. The city's population decreased by 20.2% from 2001 to 2011; the 2001 census recorded a total population of about 16,000. The female population growth rate was −8.1%, which was 19.9% higher than the male growth rate of −28%. The general caste population declined by 27.9%, the schedule caste population increased by 8.5%, and the child population decreased by 24.7% between the two censuses. In 2011, Samba had 820 females per 1,000 males, compared to the state average of 889 females per 1,000 males. For children under seven, there are 806 girls per 1,000 boys, compared to the state average of 862 girls per 1,000 boys. Between 2001 and 2011, the overall sex ratio and child sex ratio in Samba increased by 177 females per 1,000 males and 36 girls per 1,000 boys, respectively. A worker is defined as a person engaged in business, job, service, cultivation, or labor. Of the population, 4,356 (34%) are engaged in work or business activities; 91.80% are in Main Work (full-time) and 8.20% in Marginal Work (part-time). By sex, 3,885 are male workers and 471 are female workers. On 26 September 2013, militants impersonating army personnel attacked the Hiranagar Police Station. After the attack, they commandeered a truck to Samba, located 18 km (11 mi) from Hiranagar. The militants entered the army cantonment and opened fire. In a day-long operation and combat search, all three militants were killed, and twelve others, including a lieutenant colonel, were killed in the incident.
